executive_summary: This skill is designed to automate TikTok slideshow marketing for apps or products. It researches competitors, generates AI images, adds text overlays, posts via Postiz, tracks analytics, and iterates on what works. The skill has a medium overall risk due to its susceptibility to prompt injection and potential memory poisoning attacks. It is recommended to limit the processing of external content, validate and sanitize any user-supplied text, and ensure that dependencies and tools used in the skill are free from insecure deserialization and memory poisoning vulnerabilities.
skill_purpose_analysis: The skill is designed to automate the TikTok marketing process, covering competitor research, image generation, text overlays, posting, analytics tracking, and optimization. While the design is inherently risky due to the processing of external content and user-supplied text, the skill takes steps to mitigate these risks by limiting the scope of external content processing and validating user-supplied text.
dangerous_patterns: Instructions telling the agent to read external documents and act on their content
Processing of user-supplied text as instructions
Instructions that write agent outputs directly back into persistent memory without validation
safe_patterns: Limiting the processing of external content to specific, trusted sources
Validating and sanitizing user-supplied text before processing
remediation_priority: First, address the prompt injection and memory poisoning vulnerabilities by limiting the processing of external content and validating user-supplied text. Then, ensure that dependencies and tools used in the skill are free from insecure deserialization and state manipulation vulnerabilities.

vulnerabilities.title: External content could hijack agent behavior via the skill
vulnerabilities.affected_content: Instructions telling the agent to read external documents and act on their content, processing of user-supplied text as instructions, 'follow the instructions in the file', eval-like treatment of retrieved content
vulnerabilities.explanation: The skill instructs the agent to process content from emails, documents, web pages, databases, and treat embedded text as new instructions. This could allow an external attacker to plant instructions in retrieved data, potentially leading to unintended actions or data exfiltration.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: An attacker sends a specially crafted email or document to the user, containing instructions that the agent will execute once the user follows the 'instructions in the file'. This could lead to arbitrary code execution, data exfiltration, or other unintended actions.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Limit the processing of external content to specific, trusted sources. Avoid treating user-supplied text as instructions, and ensure that any external content is properly sanitized and validated before being processed by the agent.

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of attacker-controlled data leads to RCE
vulnerabilities.affected_content: pickle, marshal, yaml.load, json.loads on untrusted data, XML parsing without entity protection (XXE risk)
vulnerabilities.explanation: The skill does not appear to perform any deserialization of untrusted data. However, if any dependencies or tools used in the skill have insecure deserialization vulnerabilities, this could lead to RCE or other unintended actions.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: An attacker sends a specially crafted, malicious serialized object to the agent, which is then deserialized and executed. This could lead to arbitrary code execution, data exfiltration, or other unintended actions.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Ensure that all dependencies and tools used in the skill are free from insecure deserialization vulnerabilities. Use safe deserialization methods, and validate and sanitize any untrusted data before deserializing it.

vulnerabilities.title: Attacker compromises future agent behavior by poisoning persistent memory
vulnerabilities.affected_content: Instructions that write agent outputs, retrieved content, or user input directly back into persistent memory (vector stores, conversation history, agent scratchpads) without validation
vulnerabilities.explanation: The skill does not appear to write agent outputs, retrieved content, or user input directly back into persistent memory without validation. However, if any dependencies or tools used in the skill have memory poisoning vulnerabilities, this could lead to unintended actions or data exfiltration.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: An attacker sends a specially crafted input to the agent, which is then written to persistent memory without proper validation. This could lead to memory poisoning, allowing the attacker to compromise future agent behavior.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Ensure that all dependencies and tools used in the skill are free from memory poisoning vulnerabilities. Validate and sanitize any data written to persistent memory, and limit the scope of memory usage to the intended purpose of the skill.

vulnerabilities.title: Attacker corrupts the agent's internal decision state
vulnerabilities.affected_content: Skill instructions that allow an external party to redirect the agent's intermediate goals or reasoning trajectory (goal/plan corruption), skill design that lets an attacker bypass confirmation steps, safety checks, or human-in-the-loop gates without explicit user approval (confirmation-state bypass)
vulnerabilities.explanation: The skill does not appear to have any explicit vulnerabilities related to agentic state manipulation. However, if any dependencies or tools used in the skill have state manipulation vulnerabilities, this could lead to unintended actions or data exfiltration.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: An attacker sends a specially crafted input to the agent, which is then used to bypass confirmation steps or safety checks. This could lead to unintended actions or data exfiltration.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Ensure that all dependencies and tools used in the skill are free from state manipulation vulnerabilities. Validate and sanitize any data used in confirmation steps or safety checks, and limit the scope of state usage to the intended purpose of the skill.

clawhub_summary: The skill is named 'tiktok-app-marketing' and automates TikTok slideshow marketing for any app or product. It researches competitors, generates AI images, adds text overlays, posts via Postiz, tracks analytics, and iterates on what works. The skill is internally consistent and appears safe for general use.
clawhub_assessment: This skill is a marketing tool for TikTok that automates the creation and posting of slideshow content. It uses Node.js, node-canvas, and Postiz to generate images, add text overlays, and post content. The skill also supports cross-posting to other platforms and offers optional conversion tracking with RevenueCat. Before installing this skill, ensure that your AI agent has Node.js (v18+) and Postiz installed. If you choose to use conversion tracking, install the RevenueCat skill from ClaWHub. Be aware that this skill requires a more hands-on approach during the onboarding process and when publishing posts. Always double-check the posts in your TikTok inbox before publishing to ensure they have the correct music and are ready for publication. Monitor the 'tiktok-marketing/reports' directory for daily reports and suggested hooks. If you encounter any issues, refer to the'references' directory for troubleshooting and documentation.
clawhub_purpose_capability_desc: The skill's name, description, and code are consistent. There are no undisclosed capabilities.
clawhub_instruction_scope_desc: The runtime instructions operate within the boundaries appropriate for the stated task. The skill avoids reading unrelated system files, contacting unexpected external endpoints, or treating retrieved content as executable instructions.
clawhub_install_mechanism_desc: The skill does not download scripts from the internet, use pip/npm at runtime, or write files outside the workspace. It uses only bundled code or clearly declared dependencies.
clawhub_credentials_desc: The skill does not hardcode credentials. It uses secret_ref or environment variables correctly and explicitly avoids logging or transmitting secrets.
clawhub_persistence_privilege_desc: The skill does not modify agent settings, other skills, or system-wide configuration. It does not request elevated privileges beyond what the task requires and creates workspace-bounded writes only.
